title: Matthew Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Matthew 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil
Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights
The devil taketh Jesus up into the holy city and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple
The devil taketh Jesus up into an exceeding high mountain and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:1 states that Jesus was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil, which is the first event in the chapter.

questions.question: How long did Jesus fast before he was hungry?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:2 says Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights and was afterward hungry.

questions.question: Who came to Jesus to tempt him after his fast?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:3 refers to the tempter coming to Jesus to tempt him.

questions.question: What did the tempter ask Jesus to do with the stones?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:3 records the tempter saying, 'If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread.'

questions.question: What is Jesus' response to the tempter about living by bread?
options: Man shall live by bread alone
Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God
Bread is the staff of life
questions.correctAnswer: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:4 records Jesus answering with that exact phrase.

questions.question: Where did the devil take Jesus to set him on a pinnacle?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:5 states the devil taketh him up into the holy city and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple.

questions.question: What did the devil say would happen if Jesus cast himself down from the temple pinnacle?
options: He would be caught by angels
He would be healed by the crowd
questions.correctAnswer: He would be caught by angels
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:6 quotes the devil saying angels shall bear him up lest he dash his foot against a stone.

questions.question: What scripture does Jesus quote in response to the devil's challenge to cast himself down?
options: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God
Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:7 records Jesus saying, 'It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.'

questions.question: Where did the devil take Jesus to show him all the kingdoms of the world?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:8 says the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world.

questions.question: What did the devil promise to give Jesus if he would worship him?
options: All the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them
questions.correctAnswer: All the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:9 states the devil said he would give all these things if Jesus worshipped him.

questions.question: How many days and nights did Jesus fast according to Matthew 4?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:2 clearly states Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness in order to be tempted by the devil.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:1 states Jesus was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.

questions.question: True or False: The devil took Jesus to the top of the temple and urged him to jump to the ground.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:5-6 describe the devil taking Jesus to the pinnacle of the temple and telling him to cast himself down.

questions.question: True or False: The devil promised Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if Jesus would worship him.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:9 quotes the devil saying he would give all these things if Jesus worshipped him.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus turned the stones into bread to prove he was the Son of God.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:3-4 shows the tempter suggesting Jesus make stones bread, but Jesus does not do this; he replies with scripture instead.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell Satan regarding worship?
options: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
You can worship whoever you want.
I have no need for worship.
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Jesus explicitly states this in Matthew 4:10 in response to Satan's temptation.

questions.question: What does Matthew 4:11 promise will happen if someone resists temptation as commanded in Matthew 4:10?
options: They will be rewarded with riches.
They will never face temptation again.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Matthew 4:11 states that after Jesus resisted temptation, the devil left him.

questions.question: Where did Jesus dwell after leaving Nazareth?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Matthew 4:13 indicates that Jesus came and dwelt in Capernaum.

questions.question: Which prophet's words were fulfilled when Jesus began his ministry in Galilee according to Matthew 4:14?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Matthew 4:14 mentions that it was spoken by Esaias (Isaiah) the prophet.

questions.question: What significant event occurred in the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim according to Matthew 4:16?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Matthew 4:16 states that the people which sat in darkness saw great light.

questions.question: What message did Jesus begin to preach as recorded in Matthew 4:17?
options: Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Seek first the kingdom of God.
questions.correctAnswer: Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct since Matthew 4:17 clearly states the message Jesus preached.

questions.question: What were Simon Peter and Andrew doing when Jesus saw them?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Matthew 4:18 tells us that they were casting a net into the sea because they were fishers.

questions.question: What does Matthew 4:12 signify about the timing of Jesus' ministry?
options: It began after John was imprisoned.
It started before John baptized Him.
It was initiated by the Spirit.
It was delayed due to opposition.
questions.correctAnswer: It began after John was imprisoned.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Matthew 4:12 indicates that Jesus departed into Galilee upon hearing of John's imprisonment.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the tempter's command to turn stones into bread?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Matthew 4:4 shows that Jesus responded with the scripture, stating that man shall not live by bread alone.

questions.question: What fundamental truth about God's protection does Jesus affirm in Matthew 4:7?
options: We should not tempt the Lord our God.
questions.correctAnswer: We should not tempt the Lord our God.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Matthew 4:7 shows Jesus affirming that it is written not to tempt the Lord.

questions.question: What does Matthew 4:5-6 teach about the devil's tactics?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Matthew 4:5-6 shows the devil quoting scripture to tempt Jesus, demonstrating his deceptive tactics.

questions.question: What did the angels do after the devil left Jesus according to Matthew 4:11?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Matthew 4:11 states that angels came and ministered unto Jesus after the devil left.

questions.question: Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted. Is this statement true?
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Matthew 4:1 explicitly states that Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness.

questions.question: The devil offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world freely. Is this statement true?
questions.explanation: This statement is false because the devil's offer was contingent on Jesus worshipping him, as stated in Matthew 4:9.

questions.question: Jesus was tempted only once in the wilderness. Is this statement true?
questions.explanation: This statement is false because Jesus faced multiple temptations during his time in the wilderness, as detailed in Matthew 4:1-10.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Matthew 4:19, what does Jesus say he will make the disciples if they follow Him?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:19 states, "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men," indicating this is what Jesus promised.

questions.question: According to Matthew 4:20, how did Simon Peter and Andrew respond to Jesus' call?
options: They straightway left their nets and followed him
They asked for time to think
They went to tell others first
questions.correctAnswer: They straightway left their nets and followed him
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:20 explicitly says, "And they straightway left their nets, and followed him."

questions.question: Who were the two brothers Jesus called after Simon Peter and Andrew as mentioned in Matthew 4:21?
options: James and John, sons of Zebedee
Joseph and Judas, sons of Alphaeus
questions.correctAnswer: James and John, sons of Zebedee
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:21 identifies these two as "James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother."

questions.question: In Matthew 4:22, what did James and John do when Jesus called them?
options: They immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him
They asked for permission from their father
They sent a message back to Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: They immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states, "And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him."

questions.question: What three activities did Jesus do throughout Galilee as described in Matthew 4:23?
options: Teaching in synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, healing sickness
Leading armies, teaching law, judging disputes
Preaching repentance only, fasting, and praying
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching in synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, healing sickness
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:23 summarizes Jesus' ministry as "teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease."

questions.question: According to Matthew 4:24, from which region did Jesus' fame spread as people brought the sick to Him?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:24 says, "And his fame went throughout all Syria," indicating the widespread renown of Jesus.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'ἁμαρτάνω' (hamartanō) which appears in the thematic context of repentance in Matthew 4:17?
options: To sin or miss the mark
questions.correctAnswer: To sin or miss the mark
questions.explanation: The Greek verb 'ἁμαρτάνω' means 'to sin' or 'to miss the mark,' which relates to repentance as turning away from sin (Matthew 4:17).

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Matthew 4:19 when Jesus calls the disciples 'fishers of men'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'fishers of men' in Matthew 4:19 is a metaphor, likening the disciples' mission to fishing but for people instead of fish.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is fulfilled by Matthew 4:16's reference to 'the people which sat in darkness saw great light'?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:16 quotes Isaiah 9:2, which prophesies the coming of a great light to those in darkness.

questions.question: Which New Testament book also emphasizes the theme of Jesus calling disciples to follow Him as seen in Matthew 4:18-22?
questions.explanation: Mark 1:16-20 records Jesus calling Simon Peter, Andrew, James, and John, similar to Matthew 4:18-22.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus beginning His ministry in Galilee as recorded in Matthew 4:12?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:12 explains Jesus departed into Galilee after hearing that John was cast into prison.

questions.question: In Matthew 4:23, Jesus' ministry included healing 'all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.' What does this demonstrate in terms of typology?
options: Jesus as the Messiah fulfilling Isaiah's healing prophecies
Jesus acting only as a teacher
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus as the Messiah fulfilling Isaiah's healing prophecies
questions.explanation: The healing ministry in Matthew 4:23 fulfills Isaiah's prophecies of the Messiah bringing restoration and healing.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophetic phrase is an example of inclusio framing Jesus' ministry in Matthew 4:15 and Matthew 4:16?
options: 'Land of Zebulun and Naphtali... the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light'
'The valley of dry bones shall live again'
'Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked'
'The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone'
questions.correctAnswer: 'Land of Zebulun and Naphtali... the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light'
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:15-16 cites Isaiah 9:1-2 creating an inclusio that frames Jesus' ministry geographically and thematically.

questions.question: Jesus' refusal to turn stones into bread in Matthew 4:4 is an example of which literary device?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:4, Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 8:3, alluding to Scripture to counter temptation.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 4:25, people from beyond Jordan followed Jesus.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:25 states, "And there followed him great multitudes... from beyond Jordan."

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 4:4 teach about the source of true life and sustenance?
options: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God
Man can live by bread alone if he has faith
Physical sustenance is the ultimate source of life
Life is independent of God's word
questions.correctAnswer: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:4 states that true life depends not merely on physical sustenance but on the word of God, teaching the doctrine that spiritual nourishment through God's word is essential for human life.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' messianic identity and divine sonship is taught in Matthew 4:3?
options: Jesus' identity as Son of God is subject to temptation and testing
Jesus denies being the Son of God
Jesus accepts temptation as proof of His divine sonship
Jesus is unaware of His divine identity
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' identity as Son of God is subject to temptation and testing
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:3 shows the devil challenging Jesus' sonship, indicating that Jesus' identity as the Son of God is tested, teaching that even the Messiah undergoes temptation to fulfill His redemptive role.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the kingdom of God is taught in Matthew 4:17?
options: The kingdom of heaven is at hand and requires repentance
The kingdom of heaven is a future event with no present relevance
The kingdom is only for the Jewish people
Repentance is unrelated to the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of heaven is at hand and requires repentance
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:17 presents Jesus' proclamation that the kingdom of heaven is imminent and calls for repentance, teaching that entering God's kingdom demands a turning from sin and a readiness for God's reign.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 4:11 specifically demonstrate in the context of Jesus' temptation?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:11 shows that after the devil departs, angels come to minister to Jesus, demonstrating God's providential care and protection during the Messiah's testing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated by Jesus' use of Scripture to counter temptation in Matthew 4:7?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:7, Jesus rebukes the devil by citing Scripture, showing His holiness through refusal to sin or test God, maintaining moral purity under temptation.

questions.question: How does Jesus’ calling of fishermen in Matthew 4:18–22 prepare for the theme of Gospel mission elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It anticipates the Great Commission to become fishers of men
It contradicts later teachings on evangelism
It is a symbolic gesture without practical application
It limits the mission to the Jewish people only
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the Great Commission to become fishers of men
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:18–22 introduces the disciples’ calling to become 'fishers of men,' prefiguring the later Great Commission (Matthew 28:19–20) and emphasizing the church’s mission to evangelize.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Matthew 4:14–16 fulfill with respect to Old Testament prophecy?
options: It fulfills Isaiah’s prophecy about the light coming to Galilee of the Gentiles
It contradicts the promises made to Israel
It introduces a new covenant replacing all Old Testament covenants
It denies any connection between Jesus and Old Testament prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Isaiah’s prophecy about the light coming to Galilee of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:14–16 shows Jesus’ ministry fulfilling Isaiah’s prophecy (Isaiah 9:1–2) that the people in darkness would see a great light, linking Jesus’ work to God’s covenantal promises.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Matthew 4:10 and Matthew 4:7 teach about worship and obedience?
options: Worship and service are due to God alone, and one must not test God
Worship may be divided between God and other powers
Testing God is a legitimate expression of faith
questions.correctAnswer: Worship and service are due to God alone, and one must not test God
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:7 forbids tempting the Lord, and Matthew 4:10 commands worship of God only, together teaching exclusive worship and obedience to God without testing Him.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Matthew 4:23 and Matthew 4:24 teach about Jesus’ ministry?
options: Jesus’ ministry encompasses teaching, preaching, and healing, demonstrating the inbreaking of God’s kingdom
Jesus’ ministry is limited to preaching only
Healing is unrelated to the gospel message
Jesus performs miracles to prove political power
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ ministry encompasses teaching, preaching, and healing, demonstrating the inbreaking of God’s kingdom
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:23–24 shows Jesus teaching, preaching the kingdom, and healing, indicating the holistic nature of His ministry as God's kingdom is breaking into the world.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis do Matthew 4:1 and Matthew 4:2 provide regarding Jesus’ humanity and the role of the Spirit?
options: Jesus, though fully divine, experiences real human hunger and is led by the Spirit into testing
Jesus is only divine and does not experience human weakness
The Spirit tempts Jesus independently of His will
Jesus’ hunger is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus, though fully divine, experiences real human hunger and is led by the Spirit into testing
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:1–2 teaches that Jesus undergoes genuine human hunger and is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, highlighting His true humanity and obedience to the Spirit’s guidance.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Matthew 4:1–11 portrays Jesus succumbing to temptation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Jesus resists all temptations by relying on Scripture, showing His sinlessness
Jesus succumbs to some temptations but repents later
Temptation proves Jesus is not divine
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus resists all temptations by relying on Scripture, showing His sinlessness
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:1–11 records Jesus’ temptation and His use of Scripture to resist every temptation, affirming His sinlessness and divine mission.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 4:25 teach about the scope of Jesus’ ministry and the inclusion of diverse peoples?
options: Jesus’ ministry attracts multitudes from diverse regions, signifying the universal reach of salvation
Jesus’ ministry is confined to Galilee only
Jesus excluded Gentiles from His ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ ministry attracts multitudes from diverse regions, signifying the universal reach of salvation
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:25 shows people following Jesus from various regions including Gentile areas, indicating the universal scope of His redemptive work.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the Spirit leading Jesus into the wilderness in Matthew 4:1?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:1 shows the Spirit leading Jesus into the wilderness, demonstrating God's sovereign control over the events in Jesus’ life and mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about discipleship and calling is taught by Matthew 4:19 and Matthew 4:22?
options: Following Jesus requires immediate response and leaving behind former livelihoods and relationships
Following Jesus does not require any change in life
Jesus calls only professional religious leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Following Jesus requires immediate response and leaving behind former livelihoods and relationships
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:19 and 4:22 show Jesus calling fishermen to follow Him, who immediately leave their nets and father, teaching that discipleship demands decisive commitment and surrender.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Matthew 4:12 establish with the broader Gospel story?
options: Jesus begins His public ministry after John the Baptist’s imprisonment, signaling transition to the Messiah’s work
Jesus’ ministry is unrelated to John’s message
John’s imprisonment ends the prophetic era
Jesus begins ministry before John’s preaching
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus begins His public ministry after John the Baptist’s imprisonment, signaling transition to the Messiah’s work
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:12 marks the start of Jesus’ ministry upon hearing of John’s imprisonment, highlighting the transition from the prophetic preparation to the fulfillment in Christ.
